title: Sections with support of a constructible complex are constructible
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure
$\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in it.
Assume that $X,Z,U$ are separated schemes of finite type over $k$ and all
morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let
$\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\Qlb}$, with the condensed coefficient rings of
[sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back to each scheme
as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Write $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$
for the unbounded derived category of $\Lambda_T$-module objects and
$\Dbc(T,\Lambda)$ for its full subcategory of bounded complexes with constructible
cohomology [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible].

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with open complement
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$. Use the module-object derived functors of
[sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], writing $i^*,j^*$ for the exact derived
inverse images and $i_*$ for the exact closed direct image. Let
$R\underline\Gamma_Z$ be the right derived functor of
$M\mapsto i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$, as in [sk-lem-formal-closed-support].
For $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ the sequence
$$
i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K
\longrightarrow (i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK)[1]
$$
whose first two arrows are the counit of $i_*\dashv R\underline\Gamma_Z$
and the unit of $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ is a distinguished triangle in
$D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$. All its terms, including the shifted term,
lie in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$, and $R\underline\Gamma_ZK\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: The setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] makes $X$ a finite-type $k$-scheme. The field $k$ is Noetherian: its ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The one-point affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $X$ Noetherian. For clarity, the quasi-compactness required of the complementary open follows directly on every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$: its ring $R$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. Write $U\cap\operatorname{Spec}R=\bigcup_aD(g_a)$. The ideal generated by all $g_a$ is finitely generated, so finitely many of the original $g_a$ generate it (expand each of a finite set of generators as a finite linear combination). Their basic opens still cover the same open, so $U\cap\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a finite union of quasi-compact basic opens and is quasi-compact. Since this holds for every affine open of $X$, the definition of quasi-compact morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives that $j$ is quasi-compact. This is the Noetherian standing-scheme case required by the closed-support input, with admissible coefficients $E$ or $\Qlb$.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; blueprint proof, second paragraph: X Noetherian and j quasi-compact

proof.text: All operations use the pulled-back ring sheaves, not discrete constant field coefficients. The coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_f:f^*\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_X$ is part of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. With the module pullback of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] therefore makes $i^*$ and $j^*$ exact on module sheaves. By the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], their left derived functors are their termwise functors, which justifies writing $i^*,j^*$ for $Li^*,Lj^*$. These identifications retain the inverse-image module actions.

source.place: Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion, and open restriction; blueprint proof, restriction and pullback sentences

proof.text:
Apply [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived] to the same $X,Z,i,j,\Lambda$; its standing-scheme hypotheses hold by step 1. Part (1) gives $i_*\dashv R\underline\Gamma_Z$, and part (3) gives the natural distinguished triangle
$$i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to(i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK)[1]$$
in the ambient module-object derived category, with second arrow the unit. Its final displayed consequence also gives $R\underline\Gamma_ZK\simeq i^*\fib(K\to Rj_*j^*K)$, which will be used in step 7. No constructibility is needed for this application.

source.place: first paragraph: derived closed-support localization triangle

proof.text: We verify the counit using only the stated triangle and adjunctions; do not assume the unlabelled first arrow is already the counit. Put $G=R\underline\Gamma_ZK$, $F=i_*G$, $B=Rj_*j^*K$, and write $a:F\to K$ for that first arrow. The module identities of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] give exact $i_*$, $i^*i_*\cong\operatorname{id}$ and $j^*i_*=0$. Along with step 2 and the exact-functor rule of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], these identities hold termwise on the derived categories, with the coefficient identifications of step 2. The adjunctions of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] identify $\Hom_X(i_*A,B)$ with $\Hom_U(j^*i_*A,j^*K)=0$ for every $A\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$. Also $\Hom_X(i_*A,B[-1])\cong\Hom_X((i_*A)[1],B)\cong\Hom_X(i_*(A[1]),B)=0$, since termwise $i_*$ commutes with shifts. Exactness of Hom into a distinguished triangle [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], applied also to its inverse rotation using [def-weil-triangulated-category], shows that $a\circ-:\Hom_X(i_*A,F)\to\Hom_X(i_*A,K)$ is bijective: existence uses $\Hom_X(i_*A,B)=0$, and its kernel is the image of $\Hom_X(i_*A,B[-1])=0$. The adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$ and $i^*i_*\cong\operatorname{id}$ also identify $\Hom_Z(A,G)$ with $\Hom_X(i_*A,i_*G)$ by pushforward. Let $u:G\to G$ be the transpose of $a$ under $i_*\dashv R\underline\Gamma_Z$ from [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived]. If $\varepsilon_K:i_*G\to K$ is its counit, then $a=\varepsilon_K\circ i_*u$. More explicitly, for $h:A\to G$, naturality of $i_*\dashv R\underline\Gamma_Z$ sends $a\circ i_*h$ to $u\circ h$. Thus postcomposition by $u$ is the composite of the pushforward bijection $\Hom_Z(A,G)\cong\Hom_X(i_*A,F)$, the bijection $a\circ-$, and the adjunction bijection $\Hom_X(i_*A,K)\cong\Hom_Z(A,G)$. It is therefore bijective for every $A$. Taking $A=G$, surjectivity supplies $v$ with $uv=1$, and injectivity applied to $u(vu)=u=u1$ gives $vu=1$. Thus $u$ is invertible. If $d:B\to F[1]$ is the old connecting arrow, form the triangle with the same objects and arrows $\varepsilon_K$, the unchanged unit, and $d^{\prime}=(i_*u)[1]\circ d$. The triple $(i_*u,1_K,1_B)$ is an isomorphism from the old triangle to this one: $a=\varepsilon_K\circ i_*u$ verifies the first square, the second square is the identity square, and $(i_*u)[1]\circ d=d^{\prime}$ verifies the last square. The isomorphism axiom for distinguished triangles in [def-weil-triangulated-category] proves that this is the required triangle. The objects and fiber formula used below are unchanged.

source.place: first paragraph, final sentence: normalize the first map to the counit by the two adjunctions and Hom exactness (Stacks 09AA, 09BM; derived.tex, axioms of distinguished triangles)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dc-upper-star-preserves] with $f=j$ and input $K$. By step 2 this yields $j^*K\in\Dbc(U,\Lambda)$. Then [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves] with $f=j$ yields $Rj_*j^*K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$. Both morphisms and schemes have exactly the setting of these lemmas, and both permitted coefficients $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ occur in the direct-image statement. This existing result, bound to the unit sk-prop-open-coefficients, supplies the open-direct-image assertion cited under that unit name in the blueprint.

source.place: second paragraph: restriction and open direct-image finiteness

proof.text: The other vertex $K$ is bounded constructible by hypothesis. Since $X$ is Noetherian and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, the two-vertices clause of [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated] applies to the triangle of step 3 and makes $F=i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK$ bounded constructible. Its shift clause also gives $F[1]\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$, so every displayed term is covered.

source.place: second paragraph: triangulated closure of Dbc

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dc-upper-star-preserves] with $f=i$ and input $F=i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK$, which is bounded constructible by step 6. By step 2, $i^*F\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$. In the distinguished triangle of step 3, $F$ is a fiber of the unit $K\to Rj_*j^*K$. The fiber formula of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived] therefore identifies $R\underline\Gamma_ZK$ with $i^*F$. The isomorphism-closure clause of [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated], applied on $Z$, which is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] because $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite type and the field $k$ is Noetherian, gives $R\underline\Gamma_ZK\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$. This is the source's final pullback-and-cancellation step, using the already-stated fiber formula.

source.place: second paragraph, last sentence: recover the supported complex by closed pullback and the fiber formula
